solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Getting aide is really not a good plan?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: an absurd arrangement of the word idea gets the letters of aide

explanation.surface: Someone thinks recruiting an assistant is a poor scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'absurd' read as an anagram signal working on IDEA produces AIDE, the word in the clue. 'is really' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridiculous notion is by definition a plan nobody sensible would follow.

clue.text: TT race practice

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, and a teetotal person or place is dry
to race is to run

explanation.surface: Motorcyclists warm up before the Isle of Man TT race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'TT race' suggests the Isle of Man motorcycle event, but here TT is the abbreviation for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal held before the real event is a practice run with nothing at stake.

clue.text: Either end of chef's trolley

indicators.note: of ties the choice to the two ends, so the word or is written between the first and last letters of chef's
end, applied to both sides of chef's, means its first and last letters

parts.note: either ... or: the choice either asks for is spelt out with the word or

explanation.surface: A cook's serving cart can be pushed from whichever end you like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either end of chef' is spelt out literally as C OR F: 'end' takes the first and last letters, and 'Either' calls for the word OR between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A corf is a small wagon or basket used to carry coal in a mine, a kind of trolley.

clue.text: I've no idea what a customs officer may do

definitions.meaning: a casual phrase meaning I don't know

definitions.text: what a customs officer may do
definitions.meaning: a customs official may ask to inspect a traveller's body or bags

explanation.surface: A traveller shrugs at a question while the customs officer looks on.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a shrugging admission of ignorance; taken literally it invites a body check.

clue.text: Amaze trio before start of Vangelis number

parts.note: the three letters of the alphabet that come just before V, the first letter of Vangelis

explanation.surface: Three musicians open a Vangelis piece and dazzle the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trio' looks like three performers, but it means the three letters sitting before V in the alphabet. Vangelis is the Greek composer of the Chariots of Fire theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to astonish them so much they are left speechless.

clue.text: I can be seen smothering Rod beside the motorway — that'll stop the traffic!

indicators.note: smothering means covering all round, so the self wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: the ego is the I, the self

indicators.note: beside puts the rod next to the motorway in the charade

parts.note: M is short for motorway, as in the M1
a bar is a rod of metal

explanation.surface: A lone figure stands holding a pole by the motorway, apparently trying to halt the cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' here means trade, not cars on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade with a country, so it halts commercial dealings.

clue.text: Senior cricket player dropping first innings openers

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so these letters are taken out of the player

parts.note: a fielder is a member of the fielding side in cricket

indicators.note: the openers of words are their initial letters, here of first and innings

explanation.surface: A veteran cricketer loses his place among the openers for the first innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' sounds like opening batsmen, but it means the first letters F and I, which come out of FIELDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is someone older, a senior member of a family or community.

clue.text: Surplus old paintings sent back

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: sent back means the word for paintings is turned round

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: Unwanted old pictures are returned to the dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extra is more than is needed, a surplus amount.

clue.text: In Guinea — Susu, a language expressed in the normal way

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the answer sits inside the words Guinea, Susu, a language

explanation.surface: A note that in Guinea the Susu language is spoken in the usual manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Susu is a real West African language spoken in Guinea, which makes the surface plausible; 'expressed' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something the customary way is doing it as one always does.

clue.text: Egyptian city featured functional houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the word sits inside the words featured functional

explanation.surface: An Egyptian town shows off its practical buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun but is the verb: the phrase holds the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edfu is a city on the Nile in Upper Egypt, known for its Temple of Horus.

clue.text: Express doubt after nerd free to cast vote

indicators.note: after places the hesitation sound at the end of the rearranged letters
to cast is to throw or mould, so the letters of nerd free are formed anew

parts.note: um is the sound people make when unsure

explanation.surface: A doubtful geek is allowed to take part in a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cast vote' reads as one phrase, but 'cast' is the anagram signal and 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum is a vote by the whole electorate on a single question.

clue.text: Initially cartographer reveals perfect place for London map to be put back on shelf

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letters of cartographer and reveals

parts.note: Eden is the ideal garden, a paradise

indicators.note: put back means the letters of the map's name are turned round

parts.note: the A-Z is the classic London street atlas

explanation.surface: A mapmaker shows where the London street atlas belongs on the bookshelf.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is a well-known British street atlas, first produced for London.
explanation.definitionFit: A credenza is a sideboard or cabinet with a flat top, used like a shelf for display.

clue.text: One directs partner to bow

definitions.meaning: a pointer showing the way, as on a road sign
the shaft an archer fires from a bow

explanation.surface: A conductor points the way and has his partner take a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointing symbol on signs and the archer's missile share one name.

clue.text: He's a priest overwhelmed by a bad smell

definitions.note: He is the chemical symbol of this element, so this is what He stands for

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped, so the priest sits inside the smell

parts.note: hum is British slang for a nasty odour
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A clergyman is overcome by a dreadful stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's' looks like a pronoun but is the chemical symbol He; Eli, the Old Testament priest, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol He on the periodic table stands for this light noble gas.

clue.text: The postman's incendiary anagram indicator?

parts.note: an explosive device sent through the mail, and also a word telling the solver to blow up the letters

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter jokes about the explosive parcel a postman might carry.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive mailed in an envelope; read as an instruction, blasting the letters apart is what an anagram signal asks.

clue.text: Yours truly cuddled by short bisexual tart

indicators.note: cuddled by means held within, so the setter goes inside
short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: AC/DC is slang for bisexual
yours truly is the setter speaking of himself, me, I

explanation.surface: The setter is embraced by a promiscuous lover in a cheeky picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts AC/DC to ACD; 'tart' looks like a person but means sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid tastes sharp and sour, which is what tart describes in flavour.

clue.text: Discern reconstituted remains

indicators.note: reconstituted means rebuilt from parts, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make out what is left after something has been rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinders are the burnt residue left after a fire, its remains.

clue.text: Something that should be filled in before beginning of employment in my opinion

indicators.note: before puts the document ahead of the next letter

parts.words: Something that should be filled in
parts.note: a form is a document you complete

indicators.note: beginning of means the first letter of employment

explanation.surface: A job applicant thinks the paperwork should be completed before starting work.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is so as far as I am concerned states a personal view.

clue.text: It could be pubic hair is a superfluous ornament!

definitions.meaning: fur lower down the body, read as a joking phrase
a showy frill or flounce on a dress

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that some body hair is purely decorative.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a flounce or showy trimming on clothing, decoration nobody needs.

clue.text: Such a story is difficult to believe thanks to local extremists

definitions.text: Such a story is difficult to believe

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

indicators.note: extremists here means the letters at the extremes of local, its first and last

explanation.surface: A yarn is hard to swallow, thanks to some local radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' suggests militants but means the outer letters of 'local'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an exaggerated tale that strains credibility.

clue.text: In French, Den is being discussed

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: A French hideout is the topic of conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means literally in the air, used of matters under discussion or pending.

clue.text: The Queen's autobiography: Our Essence

definitions.meaning: a monarch using the royal we would title her life story this way

explanation.surface: A title for a royal memoir about the monarch's true nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen traditionally speaks of herself as 'we', the royal plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes our identity, and in royal speech it is a life story's natural title.

clue.text: Opposition leader heard rambling — whoops!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Opposition
rambling means wandering about, so the letters of heard are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Leader of the Opposition is caught talking nonsense and makes a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposition leader' suggests a politician but gives only O.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of mild dismay when something goes wrong.

clue.text: Two river country

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
the Ural is a river flowing from the Ural Mountains to the Caspian

explanation.surface: A land defined by a pair of rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Country as an adjective describes the countryside, as in country life.

clue.text: Don't jump first for a small time correction?

definitions.meaning: jump after someone else, taking the second turn
an extra tick added to clocks to keep them in step with the Earth

explanation.surface: Advice to a nervous parachutist, with a timekeeper's footnote.
explanation.definitionFit: Timekeepers occasionally add one extra unit to clocks to match the planet's slowing spin.

clue.text: Schools posh kids essentially avoided

indicators.note: essentially points to the core of the phrase posh kids, and avoided says that core is left out

explanation.surface: Private schools are shunned by wealthy children, at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schools' looks like places of education but means groups of whales or dolphins.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of whales or dolphins are called pods, just as fish swim in schools.

clue.text: It's a four-letter word!

parts.note: a swear word is called a four-letter word, and this one, a curse, happens to have exactly four letters

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a rude word.
explanation.definitionFit: A curse or swear word is popularly a four-letter word, and this curse really is one.

clue.text: Hitch back to opening of Yak hide

indicators.note: back means the word for a hitch is reversed

parts.note: a rub is a snag or difficulty, as in there's the rub

indicators.note: opening of means the first letter of Yak

explanation.surface: Someone ties a yak's hide to their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like an animal skin, but it is the verb meaning conceal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury something is to conceal it, often under earth.

clue.text: Turn weird, like an unsocial type

indicators.note: turn means rotate, so the two words are read in reverse

parts.note: odd means strange
as means like, in the way that

explanation.surface: Someone goes strange and becomes a loner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses ODD AS, giving SA DDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddo is British slang for a pathetic, socially inept person.

clue.text: Compiler's beginning to limp after fine adjustment to clog

indicators.note: after puts the setter and the next letter behind the adjustment

parts.note: a tram is a fine adjustment in mechanics
the compiler, the setter, refers to himself as me

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of limp

explanation.surface: The setter starts to hobble after tweaking a wooden shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clog' looks like a shoe but is the verb meaning hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To trammel is to hamper or restrict movement, as a clog was a weight hampering an animal.
